XMLDB.COMMENT: XMLDB file for the AI Router routing rules

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_rule
TABLE.COMMENT: Routing rules, evaluated in sortorder and then id order until one matches.

FIELD.NAME: name
FIELD.COMMENT: Administrator facing name. Never shown to end users.

FIELD.NAME: enabled
FIELD.COMMENT: Disabled rules are skipped without being deleted.

FIELD.NAME: sortorder
FIELD.COMMENT: Priority. Lowest is evaluated first, and is renumbered from zero on every write.

FIELD.NAME: targetid
FIELD.COMMENT: The ai_providers instance to delegate to. Deliberately not a foreign key, so that deleting a provider instance in core cannot fail.

FIELD.NAME: keysource
FIELD.COMMENT: Whose key pays for requests this rule claims: site, user or course. A column rather than a condition, because it says what to do once the rule has matched, which is the same side of the rule as the target. Holding a key is still a requirement for the rule to apply, and that is checked where the target is resolved.

FIELD.NAME: timestart
FIELD.COMMENT: Rule is not evaluated before this time. Zero means no start.

FIELD.NAME: timeend
FIELD.COMMENT: Rule is not evaluated after this time. Zero means no end.

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_condition
TABLE.COMMENT: Conditions of a rule. All of them must be met, and each one is satisfied by any of the values it holds.

FIELD.NAME: type
FIELD.COMMENT: Condition type, such as course or promptlength. One of each type per rule at most.

FIELD.NAME: configdata
FIELD.COMMENT: JSON understood only by the condition type named above.

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_price
TABLE.COMMENT: What a provider charges, as the administrator has entered it, with the date each rate took effect.

FIELD.NAME: provider
FIELD.COMMENT: Provider component. Rates belong to a provider and a model, not to an instance, since two instances of the same provider are charged alike.

FIELD.NAME: model
FIELD.COMMENT: Empty means this rate covers any model of that provider which has no rate of its own. Declared without a default, because XMLDB refuses an empty string as one.

FIELD.NAME: currency
FIELD.COMMENT: The currency the provider bills in, which every rate on the row and every cost worked out from it is in. Held per row but entered per provider, since a provider bills in one currency. Nothing converts between currencies.

FIELD.NAME: promptrate
FIELD.COMMENT: Per million prompt tokens, in the row's currency.

FIELD.NAME: completionrate
FIELD.COMMENT: Per million completion tokens.

FIELD.NAME: imagerate
FIELD.COMMENT: Per image, since image actions carry no token counts.

FIELD.NAME: timefrom
FIELD.COMMENT: When this rate took effect. A request is costed with the latest rate in force at the time.

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_target
TABLE.COMMENT: Per delegation target settings for bring your own key: where a key goes, and whether the site lets anybody bring one here. The name of the field a key goes in differs from provider to provider, so it is guessed and then confirmed by an administrator rather than assumed.

FIELD.NAME: targetid
FIELD.COMMENT: The ai_providers instance. Not a foreign key, so that deleting a provider instance in core cannot fail.

FIELD.NAME: keyfield
FIELD.COMMENT: Which of the instance config keys holds the key. Empty means the administrator has confirmed this provider takes no key at all, which is different from not having been asked yet. Declared without a default, because XMLDB refuses an empty string as one.

FIELD.NAME: byokmode
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether this site lets people bring a key to this provider: allowed, disallowed, or only, meaning the provider may be reached with a brought key and not with the site's own. Separate from keyfield, which says where a key goes and is a fact about the provider rather than a decision of the site's.

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_key
TABLE.COMMENT: Keys brought by a user or registered for a course, encrypted with the site key. One key per subject and delegation target. Carries the limit the owner has put on their own spending, which is theirs to set and nobody else's.

FIELD.NAME: scope
FIELD.COMMENT: Whose key it is: user or course.

FIELD.NAME: scopeid
FIELD.COMMENT: The user id or the course id, according to the scope.

FIELD.NAME: targetid
FIELD.COMMENT: The ai_providers instance this key is for. Keys belong to an instance rather than to a provider plugin, because two instances of one plugin can point at different endpoints.

FIELD.NAME: walletid
FIELD.COMMENT: The wallet this key's spending is counted against. A key rotated within the same provider account keeps its wallet; a key for another account gets a new one. The owner says which, because the key itself does not.

FIELD.NAME: secret
FIELD.COMMENT: The key, encrypted with core\encryption. Never logged, never exported and never shown again.

FIELD.NAME: hint
FIELD.COMMENT: The last few characters, so that the owner can recognise which key this is without anything being decrypted. Deliberately the end of the key: the beginning is often a fixed prefix. Declared without a default, because XMLDB refuses an empty string as one.

FIELD.NAME: timeverified
FIELD.COMMENT: When the key was last tested against the provider. Zero means never.

FIELD.NAME: verifystatus
FIELD.COMMENT: What that test said.

FIELD.NAME: capamount
FIELD.COMMENT: A limit the owner has set on their own spending at this key, in the site currency. Null means they have set none. Estimated from the site rate table, not from what the provider actually billed.

FIELD.NAME: capperiod
FIELD.COMMENT: How the limit is counted: a calendar month, or a rolling number of days.

FIELD.NAME: capdays
FIELD.COMMENT: How many days a rolling limit counts. Ignored for a calendar month.

FIELD.NAME: usermodified
FIELD.COMMENT: Who registered it. For a course key this is the only personal data in the row, and it is what a deletion request clears.

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_wallet
TABLE.COMMENT: What a brought key's spending is counted against. A provider bills an account, and the key is only the way in: rotating the key does not start a new bill, while a key for another account does. Nothing in a key says which, so the owner is asked, and the answer is kept here as which wallet a key belongs to. A wallet outlives its key, so that a key registered again after being removed can go on with the record it had.

FIELD.NAME: scope
FIELD.COMMENT: Whose it is: user or course, as on the key.

FIELD.NAME: targetid
FIELD.COMMENT: The ai_providers instance, as on the key. A wallet is for one account at one provider.

FIELD.NAME: hint
FIELD.COMMENT: The last few characters of the key held last, so that the owner can be told which record they would be going on with. Declared without a default, because XMLDB refuses an empty string as one.

FIELD.NAME: timereleased
FIELD.COMMENT: When the key holding this wallet was removed or replaced by one for another account. Zero while a key holds it.

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_walletkey
TABLE.COMMENT: Every key a wallet has held, as a keyed hash of each. It is how a key entered again is known to be one the wallet held, after the key itself has been replaced or removed, so that the same key always goes back to the same wallet. A hash cannot be turned back into the key.

FIELD.NAME: keyhash
FIELD.COMMENT: The keyed hash of one key the wallet held, in hexadecimal.

FIELD.NAME: timecreated
FIELD.COMMENT: When the wallet first held the key.

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_notice
TABLE.COMMENT: What has already been said about a budget or a key limit, so that a daily task does not say it again every day. A row exists while a threshold is over; it is removed once the spending falls back under it, which is what makes a new month start the count again without anything having to know about months.

FIELD.NAME: kind
FIELD.COMMENT: What the limit is about: the site, a course, a person, or one brought key.

FIELD.NAME: subjectid
FIELD.COMMENT: The course, person or key. Zero for the site, which has only one.

FIELD.NAME: metric
FIELD.COMMENT: What the limit counted: money, or requests. Part of the key, because the same subject can be held to a limit of each kind and they are reached at different moments.

FIELD.NAME: provider
FIELD.COMMENT: The provider a limit in money was about, since money is counted per provider. A dash for a limit in requests. Part of the key, because one subject can be held to a limit at each of two providers.

FIELD.NAME: limitamount
FIELD.COMMENT: The limit this was about. Part of the key, because one subject can have several budgets set on it by different rules.

FIELD.NAME: threshold
FIELD.COMMENT: Which share of the limit was crossed, as a percentage. An early warning and the limit itself are told apart by this.

FIELD.NAME: periodstart
FIELD.COMMENT: The start of the stretch of time the limit was about, for a limit measured over a calendar month. Zero for a rolling period, whose start moves every day and would otherwise make this say something new each morning. Part of the key, so that February gets its own answer rather than inheriting January's.

FIELD.NAME: perioddays
FIELD.COMMENT: How many days a rolling period covers. Zero for a calendar month. Part of the key, because the same subject can be held to the same amount over two different stretches of time and they are reached at different moments.

INDEX.NAME: kind-subjectid-metric-provider-limitamount-threshold-periodstart-perioddays
INDEX.FIELDS: kind, subjectid, metric, provider, limitamount, threshold, periodstart, perioddays

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_request
TABLE.COMMENT: One row per AI request the router handled, from the moment it arrived. Says who asked, where, for what, and how it ended; what was tried on its behalf is in local_airouter_attempt. The two are kept apart so that a request is always one row however many providers it took, which is what a budget counted in requests needs, and so that every provider call leaves a row of its own, which is what a bill needs.

FIELD.NAME: correlation
FIELD.COMMENT: An identifier made when the request was opened, so that a row written twice by a retried process is the same row and not a second request.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: Resolved the same way the rule engine resolves it. Null when the request came from outside any course, which is not the convention core adopted for its own register in 5.3 (-1 there), and is not translated: the two are compared, not merged.

FIELD.NAME: actionname
FIELD.COMMENT: The action basename, matching what core records.

FIELD.NAME: ruleid
FIELD.COMMENT: The rule that claimed the request, if one did.

FIELD.NAME: rulename
FIELD.COMMENT: Copied because rules get renamed and deleted, and a record nobody can read is not a record.

FIELD.NAME: keysource
FIELD.COMMENT: Whose key the request was to be paid for with: site, user or course. What each attempt was actually paid for with is on the attempt, and can differ when the chain fell back.

FIELD.NAME: state
FIELD.COMMENT: open while being worked on; then succeeded, declined (turned down before anything was tried) or failed (tried, and nothing answered).

FIELD.NAME: reason
FIELD.COMMENT: Why it did not succeed, in terms an administrator can act on.

FIELD.NAME: answeredby
FIELD.COMMENT: The target whose answer was used. Null unless the request succeeded.

FIELD.NAME: attempts
FIELD.COMMENT: How many targets were tried. A convenience: the attempt rows are the record.

FIELD.NAME: timeended
FIELD.COMMENT: When the outcome was written. Null while open. This, not timestarted, is the day a request is counted in.

FIELD.NAME: applied
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether the summary has counted this row yet. Kept on the row rather than as a watermark in the settings, so that nothing about what has been counted depends on how a setting is read.

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_attempt
TABLE.COMMENT: One row per provider the router asked on behalf of a request, whether or not it answered. What a provider charged for is charged whether it answered or not, and to whoever's key it was asked with, so each attempt carries its own target, payer, usage and cost.

FIELD.NAME: seq
FIELD.COMMENT: Which attempt of the request this is, from one. Unique with the request, so that a retried write cannot make a second attempt out of the same call.

FIELD.NAME: targetname
FIELD.COMMENT: Copied, for the same reason the rule name is copied on the request.

FIELD.NAME: targetprovider
FIELD.COMMENT: The component of the instance, which is what prices are looked up by.

FIELD.NAME: keysource
FIELD.COMMENT: Whose key this attempt was made with.

FIELD.NAME: keyid
FIELD.COMMENT: Which brought key, when one was used. Never the key itself.

FIELD.NAME: walletid
FIELD.COMMENT: The wallet the brought key charged, which is what a limit on the key is measured by. Zero when the site's own key paid.

FIELD.NAME: state
FIELD.COMMENT: started until the target comes back; then succeeded, empty, failed, threw, or lost when nothing ever came back.

FIELD.NAME: prompttokens
FIELD.COMMENT: Null when the target did not say, which is not the same as none.

FIELD.NAME: usageknown
FIELD.COMMENT: One when the token counts can be believed as counts. A report adds up the attempts where this is one and says how many it left out.

FIELD.NAME: cost
FIELD.COMMENT: Worked out when the attempt ended, never recalculated. Null when no rate was known, which is not free.

FIELD.NAME: unpriced
FIELD.COMMENT: One when the ending was written without the record lock, so that its cost is still to be worked out by whoever next holds the lock. Not counted into the summary until it is. Zero for an ending priced as it was written, including one no rate covered.

FIELD.NAME: timeended
FIELD.COMMENT: When the outcome was written. Null while started. The day an attempt is counted in.

FIELD.NAME: applied
FIELD.COMMENT: Whether the summary has counted this row yet.

TABLE.NAME: local_airouter_summary
TABLE.COMMENT: A day of the request and attempt records, added up, so that reports outlive the detail the purge removes. Built by adding each finished request and attempt into its day once and marking it applied, so that what has been counted is a fact on the row and not a watermark in the settings. Names the user for the same reason the older summary does: a site asked to account for its AI spending has to be able to say who spent it.

FIELD.NAME: daystart
FIELD.COMMENT: Midnight of the day summarised, in the server timezone. The day a fact belongs to is the day it ended.

FIELD.NAME: courseid
FIELD.COMMENT: Zero for requests made outside any course. Not null, because a unique index over a nullable column is not unique.

FIELD.NAME: targetid
FIELD.COMMENT: For an attempt, the target asked. For a request, the target that answered, or zero when none did, which is how refusals and total failures are counted.

FIELD.NAME: targetname
FIELD.COMMENT: Carried over from the attempt, because once the detail is purged this is the only readable name left.

FIELD.NAME: targetprovider
FIELD.COMMENT: The provider plugin behind the target. Part of the key, because money is added up by provider: a provider bills in one currency, and money is never added across providers. Kept here rather than looked up, since a target can be deleted. A dash for rows with no target. Shorter than the attempt table gives the same name, because a composed index has a length limit and no component name approaches sixty characters.

FIELD.NAME: model
FIELD.COMMENT: The model that answered, or a dash where none did or none was named.

FIELD.NAME: keysource
FIELD.COMMENT: Who paid. Part of the key, so that what people spent out of their own pocket is never added into what the site spent.

FIELD.NAME: walletid
FIELD.COMMENT: The wallet a brought key charged, carried from the attempt; for a request, the wallet of the attempt that answered. Part of the key, so that a limit on a key can be measured from the summary after the detail is gone. Zero when the site paid or nothing answered.

FIELD.NAME: currency
FIELD.COMMENT: The currency the money on the row is in, which is the provider's. Part of the key so that unlike figures are never added. A dash for rows carrying no money.

FIELD.NAME: requests
FIELD.COMMENT: Requests that ended that day, whatever the outcome.

FIELD.NAME: failures
FIELD.COMMENT: Of those, the ones that did not succeed: declined or failed.

FIELD.NAME: calls
FIELD.COMMENT: Attempts that ended that day, whatever the outcome. A request that fell through to a second provider is one request and two calls.

FIELD.NAME: knowncalls
FIELD.COMMENT: Of the calls, the ones whose token counts were reported. The token totals are totals of these alone.

FIELD.NAME: images
FIELD.COMMENT: Images the calls produced. Kept so that a day's cost can be worked out again, images included, when a provider's provisional currency is corrected.

FIELD.NAME: cost
FIELD.COMMENT: The costs recorded on the attempts added up. Worked out again only when the provider's currency is corrected, and then from the day's tokens and images at the rate in force that day. Only as complete as costedcalls says.

FIELD.NAME: costedcalls
FIELD.COMMENT: Of the calls, the ones that had a cost. Without it a total cannot be told apart from a total of the few calls a rate happened to cover.

INDEX.NAME: key
INDEX.FIELDS: daystart, userid, courseid, actionname, targetprovider, targetid, model, keysource, walletid, currency
